Cyrillic or Greek letters returned for a Latin word or a digit (1 → А, д, я)
the number is absent from the Archive text
one edit span, a classical-engine pair: li↔h, rn↔m, c↔e, u↔n, l↔I …
one edit span of ≤ 2 characters not in the known table
several spans, still ≤ 34% of the word
aligned slot holds a different word: a real misread of most of the word, or alignment noise
ſ/s read as f or f as s (pre-1800 typography)
proper nouns and sentence-initial words misread or dropped
a word (in a run < 8) present in the model reading, absent from the Archive text altogether
a word the Archive has, but unaligned — read in another order (columns, captions, tables)
a number the Archive has, but in another position
a readable word only the Archive has — the MODEL may have dropped it
a 1–2 letter or vowel-less fragment only in the Archive text (speckle, rules, marks read as text)
same letters, different word boundaries ("Bos ton", "ofthe")
a footnote superscript one side kept and the other dropped (convention)
a superscript read as a full-size digit (convention)
a replace block of 2+ slots, mostly unrelated words: local misalignment, not counted as misreads
same letters, different case: small caps and display type (convention, not error)
one side keeps ſ, the other normalises to s (convention)
apostrophe or hyphen form differs inside the word (convention)
accent present on one side only
a run of ≥ 8 model words absent from the Archive: caption, footnote, a column, a paragraph
a run of ≥ 8 Archive words absent from the model: the MODEL omitted it, or the Archive read the facing page
≤ 20% fragments: in the verified cases the MODEL skipped lines between repeated phrases
> 20% fragments: dot-leader tables, rules, ornaments, drop caps read as letters

rates.meaning: a 4-digit year in the model reading that the Archive read differently or not at all
digit substitution, digit↔letter, wrong digit count, or the number absent
same digits, different word boundary ("191 7", "18541855") — invisible to date search
same digit count, one or more digits differ (3↔8, 9↔0 …)
a printed number with a digit read as a letter (1855 → r855, 1st → Ist, 551 → SSI)
a printed letter read as a digit (O for Ohio → 0, Ill → 111)
Cyrillic or Greek letters returned for a Latin word or a digit (1 → А, д, я)
the number is absent from the Archive text
one edit span, a classical-engine pair: li↔h, rn↔m, c↔e, u↔n, l↔I …
one edit span of ≤ 2 characters not in the known table
several spans, still ≤ 34% of the word
aligned slot holds a different word: a real misread of most of the word, or alignment noise
ſ/s read as f or f as s (pre-1800 typography)
proper nouns and sentence-initial words misread or dropped
a word (in a run < 8) present in the model reading, absent from the Archive text altogether
a word the Archive has, but unaligned — read in another order (columns, captions, tables)
a number the Archive has, but in another position
a readable word only the Archive has — the MODEL may have dropped it
a 1–2 letter or vowel-less fragment only in the Archive text (speckle, rules, marks read as text)
same letters, different word boundaries ("Bos ton", "ofthe")
a footnote superscript one side kept and the other dropped (convention)
a superscript read as a full-size digit (convention)
a replace block of 2+ slots, mostly unrelated words: local misalignment, not counted as misreads
same letters, different case: small caps and display type (convention, not error)
one side keeps ſ, the other normalises to s (convention)
apostrophe or hyphen form differs inside the word (convention)
accent present on one side only
a run of ≥ 8 model words absent from the Archive: caption, footnote, a column, a paragraph
a run of ≥ 8 Archive words absent from the model: the MODEL omitted it, or the Archive read the facing page
≤ 20% fragments: in the verified cases the MODEL skipped lines between repeated phrases
> 20% fragments: dot-leader tables, rules, ornaments, drop caps read as letters

rates.cls: … displaced (page also has a model-only block)
rates.meaning: the same passage placed differently by the two readers (drop cap, sidebar, column): not an omission
bag agreement ≥ 0.70 but sequence agreement ≥ 0.15 lower: same words, different order
the two readings share < 55% vocabulary or differ > 30% in length — structural, not glyph-level
edge lines stripped from the Archive text as running heads or page numbers before alignment
a running head, page number or signature the model tagged is untagged body text in the Archive (it always is — this measures how often the Archive kept it at all)
